holidays.name: National Hot Buttered Rum Day
holidays.description: A toasty salute to the cozy winter cocktail made of rum, butter, brown sugar, and warming spices, stirred into hot water or cider. It is the ideal excuse to hide from the cold with a mug in hand.
holidays.origin: Hot buttered rum dates back to colonial America, where rum was plentiful and winters were harsh. The unofficial day is part of the modern wave of food and drink observances that celebrate seasonal favorites.
holidays.funFact: Hot buttered rum was a popular drink in colonial New England because rum was cheaper and easier to get than many other spirits, thanks to the molasses trade.

holidays.name: Kid Inventors' Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the creativity of young inventors and encourage kids to build, tinker, and dream up wild new gadgets. Think of it as a salute to the ideas adults never thought of.
holidays.origin: It was created by the Noodle Kidoodle toy company and the Kid Inventors' Day organization in 2001 to honor Benjamin Franklin's birthday (January 17, 1706) and to inspire young people to be inventive.
holidays.funFact: Twelve-year-old Frank Epperson invented the Popsicle by accident in 1905 after leaving a cup of soda with a stirring stick outside on a freezing night.

holidays.name: Popeye the Sailor Man Day
holidays.description: A day for spinach lovers and cartoon fans to celebrate the squinty, pipe-smoking sailor who gets super strength from a can of leafy greens. Flex those biceps and say 'I yam what I yam!'
holidays.origin: Popeye debuted in the Thimble Theatre comic strip on January 17, 1929, created by E.C. Segar. He quickly overshadowed the strip's original stars and became a pop culture icon.
holidays.funFact: Popeye's popularity was credited with boosting U.S. spinach consumption by about a third during the 1930s, and the town of Crystal City, Texas, even built a statue of him.

holidays.name: Answer Your Cat's Questions Day
holidays.description: A playful observance encouraging cat owners to give their feline overlords the courtesy of a proper answer when they meow, stare, or knock things off tables. Expect a lot of conversations about why dinner is late.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, internet-era pet holiday that grew out of the playful idea that cats are always demanding explanations from their humans.
holidays.funFact: Adult cats rarely meow at each other and mostly use meows to communicate with humans, so your cat really is talking to you.

holidays.name: Ditch New Year's Resolutions Day
holidays.description: A guilt-free day to give yourself permission to abandon the resolutions you made two weeks ago and start fresh without the pressure.
holidays.origin: Often referred to as Quitter's Day or Ditch Your Resolutions Day, it falls around the time when studies suggest many people give up on their goals, which is typically the second or third Friday of January.
holidays.funFact: Fitness-tracking data from the app Strava suggested the second Friday of January is when most people quit their resolutions, which led to the nickname Quitter's Day.
